content.title: About
content.content: An empanada is a traditional Latin American pastry consisting of a folded dough pocket filled with various ingredients. This version is stuffed with chicken breast, fresh vegetables (tomato, bell pepper, onion) and aromatic spices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Empanadas originated in Spain and were brought to Latin America by colonizers.
There are countless filling variations, from beef and cheese to sweet fruit versions.
Traditionally they are baked, but they are also frequently deep‑fried for a crisp crust.
In Argentina empanadas are a common accompaniment to mate.
The name comes from the Spanish verb “empanar,” meaning “to wrap in dough.”

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken provides a complete source of protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The vegetables add vitamin C, vitamin A and potassium, supporting immunity and blood pressure regulation.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: When baked, empanadas contain less saturated fat than fried versions, making them more heart‑friendly.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Vegetables and whole‑grain dough (if used) increase dietary fiber, aiding digestion.

items.title: Sustained energy
items.content: The blend of protein, carbohydrates and a modest amount of fat provides lasting satiety.

items.title: Allergy to chicken or gluten
items.content: People with chicken or gluten allergies should choose a gluten‑free dough alternative.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salt added to the dough and filling can raise sodium intake; monitor seasoning levels.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Empanadas can be calorie‑dense due to dough and oil, so portion control is advised for weight‑managed diets.

items.title: Proper cooking
items.content: Undercooked empanadas may contain raw chicken, increasing the risk of foodborne illness.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve empanadas hot, either as a snack on their own or with a dipping sauce such as salsa, yogurt dip, or guacamole. They are convenient for on‑the‑go meals.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked empanadas in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a freezer‑safe bag – they retain flavor and texture for up to 2 months. Reheat in the oven or microwave before eating.
